name: Companies Act 2014 — Director Duties + Compliance Statement (ss.223-225)

articles.title: Acknowledgement of duties on appointment
articles.requirement: On appointment as a director of an Irish company, the person must acknowledge in writing that they have legal duties + obligations imposed by the Companies Act, other statutes + at common law. Standard form acknowledgement retained by the company.

articles.title: Directors' compliance statement (annual)
articles.requirement: Directors of large + PIE companies must include in their directors' report an annual compliance statement: (a) acknowledging responsibility for securing compliance with 'relevant obligations' (tax law + Companies Act provisions, the breach of which would attract serious sanction); (b) confirming a compliance policy statement has been drawn up; (c) confirming appropriate arrangements + structures have been put in place to secure material compliance; (d) confirming a review of those arrangements + structures has been conducted during the financial year.

articles.title: Section 224 — scope (large companies + PIEs)
articles.requirement: Applies to private companies limited by shares + designated activity companies whose balance sheet total exceeds €12.5 million AND turnover exceeds €25 million in the financial year, plus public limited companies + public-interest entities (subject to specified carve-outs).

articles.title: Statement of Directors' Duties (codified)
articles.requirement: Eight codified fiduciary + general duties of directors: (1) act in good faith in what the director considers to be the company's interests; (2) act honestly + responsibly in relation to the company's affairs; (3) act in accordance with the company's constitution + exercise powers only for lawful purposes; (4) not use company property / information / opportunities for personal benefit (or benefit of others) unless approved by the company's constitution or members; (5) not agree to restrict the director's power to exercise independent judgment unless expressly permitted; (6) avoid conflicts between the director's duties + personal interests; (7) exercise the care + skill that may reasonably be expected of a person with the director's knowledge + experience; (8) have regard to the interests of members (in addition to creditors / employees as required by other provisions).

articles.title: Section 225 — civil consequences
articles.requirement: Breach of the duties at s.225(1) is enforceable in the same manner as a breach of fiduciary duty (and the duty at (7) as a breach of the duty of care). Civil consequences: account of profits, restoration of property, damages, declaration of the validity of contracts. The duties are owed by the director to the company.

articles.title: Interplay with SEAR Prescribed Responsibilities
articles.requirement: The s.224 compliance statement + the SEAR MRM + the SEAR Prescribed Responsibilities should describe a single coherent governance architecture. Directors' compliance-statement arrangements are typically operationalised by allocating ownership to PCFs through the MRM (PR1 risk-management, PR2 ICAAP, PR4 financial-crime, PR9 conduct, etc.) so a single set of evidence supports both regimes.

articles.title: Interplay with Common + Additional Conduct Standards
articles.requirement: The s.225 director duties + the SEAR Common + Additional Conduct Standards overlap substantially: skill/care/diligence (CA s.225(7) + CS skill/care); honesty + integrity (CA s.225(1)/(2) + CS honesty); avoidance of conflicts (CA s.225(6) + CS market conduct). Director conduct that breaches both regimes may attract both civil consequences (CA) + CBI administrative sanctions (SEAR / Conduct Standards / F&P).

articles.title: Interplay with CPC 2026 Effective Governance
articles.requirement: CPC 2026 Effective Governance Arrangements (Conduct Regs Pt III) require board / senior management responsibility for embedding Securing Customer Interests outcomes — including MI + outcome monitoring + at-least-annual board review. The same board-level processes used to evidence s.224 compliance + SEAR Prescribed Responsibilities can satisfy the CPC 2026 governance obligation, provided customer-outcomes data is integrated into the MI.
